name: USSF-627
destination_explanation: It starts around 160 km up and runs to about 2,000 km. At this height a satellite goes all the way around the planet in about an hour and a half.
slot_a_text: B1103 has six flights behind it, in six months. The mix: three Starlink, two SDA Tranche, and one NROL. At its fastest it was back on the pad in 26 days.
slot_b_text: Ion thrusters can produce only about as much thrust as the weight of a sheet of paper, but can run continuously for months or years.

lg_slot_b_text: It has already slipped five times. The current time was set in the last few hours and has held since. There is a 4-hour window to work with.
lg_slot_c_text: SLC-4E has flown 307 launches since its first in 1964, 70 of them this year. Its previous launch was 4 days earlier.
description: A classified mission for the United States Space Force. It is possibly a batch of classified LEO satellites based on SpaceX’s Starshield satellite bus, based on locations of rocket stage drop zones being exact fits with previous Starlink Group 15 launches.
